1. Where Payment Starts & Intake API Actual Implementation

Payment starts when a customer selects food items and taps "Pay via Paytm" in the client application. The frontend issues an authenticated HTTP POST request to:

POST /order/checkout/paytm-session

  • Validation: Backend validates authenticated user (user_id), outlet active state, operating hours, and cart item availability.
  • Pessimistic Order Snapshot: Inserts a row into orders with status awaiting_payment and inserts line items into order_items.
  • Payment Record Initialization: Inserts a corresponding row into payments with status PENDING, linking order_id and amount.

2. Communicating with Paytm & Token Return Paytm Official

The backend acts as the secure mediator to avoid exposing credentials:

  • Payload Generation: Prepares order payload containing Merchant ID (PAYTM_MID), unique orderId, transaction amount, and callback URL.
  • Cryptographic Signing: Calculates HMAC-SHA256 signature using the secret PAYTM_MERCHANT_KEY.
  • Paytm Response: Paytm returns a transaction token (txnToken). The backend forwards this token, orderId, and amount to the client to initialize Paytm Checkout JS / Custom UI.

3. Gateway Communication Back & Verification Actual Implementation

When payment completes or terminates at Paytm:

  • Primary Channel (Webhook): Paytm sends an asynchronous HTTPS POST request directly to POST /webhooks/paytm. This server-to-server (S2S) notification contains the gateway reference (TXNID), status (STATUS: TXN_SUCCESS), and response signature.
  • Checksum Verification: FastAPI executes _paytm_verify_checksum() to prevent payload spoofing before processing.
  • Fallback Polling: If the webhook is delayed or dropped, the client or background reconciliation queries POST /admin/payments/reconcile calling Paytm's /v3/order/status API.

4. State Persistence & Order Confirmation Actual Implementation

Final authority resides in the database, never the client:

  • Atomic Stored Procedure: Backend calls PostgreSQL procedure verify_and_record_payment().
  • Storage: Status is recorded in payments.status (SUCCESS), recording paytm_txn_id and paid_at = NOW().
  • Stock Decrement: Acquired row locks (FOR UPDATE) decrement item stock atomically.
  • Order Confirmation: Order status transitions from awaiting_payment to confirmed, generating the kitchen token for KDS tracking.

Architectural Principles & Guarantees

Zero Client Trust: The client application is strictly treated as an untrusted presentation layer. Only cryptographically verified S2S webhooks or direct backend-to-Paytm queries can confirm payments.
Strict Idempotency: Handled at database level via unique constraints on paytm_txn_id. Repeated webhook dispatches exit cleanly without duplicate order generation.
Automatic Remediation: If payment succeeds but stock has depleted or outlet is closed, the system initiates an automated refund via Paytm Refund API.

Page 2 — How Paytm Connects to the Backend

Server-to-Server Protocols, Cryptographic Signatures & Entity Correlation

1. API-Level Handshake & Communication Flow Actual Implementation

Step 1: Frontend Request
Client calls POST /order/checkout/paytm-session passing outlet_id, items array, and delivery metadata.
→
Step 2: Backend → Paytm
FastAPI constructs parameters, formats paytm_order_id, signs with HMAC-SHA256, and calls Paytm Initiate API.
→
Step 3: Paytm Token Return
Paytm validates signature & returns txnToken. Backend returns token & MID to frontend for checkout rendering.
→
Step 4: Customer Payment
Customer completes auth at Paytm. Paytm dispatches S2S webhook to /webhooks/paytm.

2. Payload Details & Gateway Endpoints Paytm Official

Paytm Host URLs:

  • Staging / Test: https://securegw-stage.paytm.in
  • Production: https://securegw.paytm.in

Initiate Transaction Endpoint:

POST /theia/api/v1/initiateTransaction?mid={mid}&orderId={orderId}

Critical Body Parameters Transmitted:

  • mid: Merchant Identifier provisioned in Paytm Dashboard.
  • orderId: Unique transaction tracking string generated by V Foods.
  • txnAmount.value & currency: Stringified amount (e.g., "250.00") and "INR".
  • userInfo.custId: Unique customer identifier (user_id).
  • callbackUrl: Backend webhook target (https://api.vfoods.in/webhooks/paytm).

3. Security, Authentication & Correlation Actual Implementation

Cryptographic Signing (HMAC-SHA256):

  • The backend utilizes _paytm_generate_checksum() to sign the JSON body string using the secret PAYTM_MERCHANT_KEY.
  • Signature is transmitted in the HTTP payload header under head.signature.
  • Credential Isolation: The secret key resides strictly in server environment variables (PAYTM_MERCHANT_KEY). It is never sent to the browser or embedded in client code.

Local Order Correlation:

  • When a checkout session is initiated, paytm_order_id is deterministically linked to local orders.id via the payments record.
  • When Paytm dispatches a webhook or status response, the backend reads ORDERID, fetches the row from payments WHERE paytm_order_id = ORDERID, and resolves the parent order_id.

V Foods • Technical Architecture Whitepaper Page 3 — Status Lifecycle & Webhook Idempotency

Page 3 — Payment Status, Webhooks & Status APIs

Multi-Channel Status Verification, Server-to-Server Webhooks & Active Recovery

1. Status Communication Channels Compared Paytm Official

  1. Frontend Payment Response (Client-side): User interface callback fired via JavaScript SDK upon redirect. Inherently untrusted. Subject to browser crashes, network drops, packet spoofing, and malicious tampering. Never used to confirm orders.
  2. Paytm Callback (Browser POST Redirect): Browser-redirected POST to CALLBACK_URL. Can fail if the user closes their mobile browser or switches apps before the redirect cycle completes.
  3. Paytm Webhook (Server-to-Server Asynchronous POST): Direct HTTPS POST from Paytm infrastructure to V Foods backend (/webhooks/paytm). Authoritative channel. Cryptographically signed, decoupled from client network health, and retried automatically by Paytm on network errors.
  4. Transaction Status API (Active Pull Mechanism): Outbound S2S query from FastAPI to Paytm's /v3/order/status endpoint. Used as active reconciliation when webhooks are delayed.

2. Why Backend Rejects Frontend Authority Best Practice

In production systems, clients are untrusted agents. Relying on frontend confirmations creates fatal attack vectors:

  • Man-in-the-Middle Spoofing: An attacker can intercept client responses and inject fake 200 OK success payloads.
  • Premature Browser Termination: If a customer closes the tab after bank debit but before the redirect fires, the order remains unpaid without S2S webhooks.
  • Dual Execution: Flaky mobile connections can re-trigger payment callbacks, leading to duplicate database records.

V Foods Enforcement: The frontend only updates UI to "Verifying Payment..." and polls the backend until the S2S webhook confirms the order.

[Payment State Uncertain: PENDING > 2 mins]
↓ User Poll OR Background Reconcile Cron

↓ S2S Query: /v3/order/status

If Valid: Confirm Order via verify_and_record_payment()
If Expired/Out of Stock: Initiate Auto-Refund via /refund/apply

5. Webhook Idempotency Guarantees Actual Implementation

Paytm guarantees "at least once" webhook delivery. Under network congestion, Paytm will retry the identical webhook payload up to 5 times. The V Foods backend enforces strict idempotency at the database engine level via PostgreSQL:

1. Unique Transaction Key: payments.paytm_txn_id is constrained with a UNIQUE index. Attempting to insert a duplicate gateway transaction ID raises a constraint violation.
2. Stored Procedure Guard: In verify_and_record_payment(), the procedure first inspects payments.status. If already SUCCESS, it exits immediately and returns existing status.
3. Stock & Order Protection: Because the procedure exits early on duplicates, stock decrement logic and order confirmation events execute strictly once. Duplicate webhooks cannot double-decrement stock or re-credit wallets.

V Foods • Technical Architecture Whitepaper Page 5 — Failure Recovery & Automated Refunds

Page 5 — Payment Success, Failure & Refunds

Handling Uncertain Transaction States, Network Dropouts & The Automated Refund Engine

1. The Primary Real-World Failure: "The Ghost Payment" Actual Implementation

Phase 1: Money Debited
Customer completes UPI/OTP. Paytm successfully debits ₹250 from customer bank.
→
Phase 2: Transit Failure
Mobile cellular drops, user closes browser tab, or AWS/V Foods restart drops incoming webhook.
→
Phase 3: Uncertain State
Paytm shows SUCCESS; V Foods database has payment marked PENDING. Customer sees no order confirmation.

2. Two-Pronged Automated Recovery Actual Implementation

The system resolves ghost payments through two active recovery loops:

  • Path A: Paytm Webhook Retry: Paytm’s S2S notification engine monitors HTTP responses. If V Foods returned a 500 error or was temporarily unreachable, Paytm automatically re-transmits the webhook at exponential backoff intervals.
  • Path B: Active Reconciler & User Poll: When customer views order tracker, frontend calls POST /order/{id}/check-payment-status. Simultaneously, background cron calls POST /admin/payments/reconcile querying Paytm's /v3/order/status API for any pending transaction older than 2 minutes.

Resolution Logic: Once Paytm returns TXN_SUCCESS, the backend inspects order validity. If the order is within the 10-minute window and stock is intact, the order is confirmed. If expired or unfulfillable, it triggers an automated refund.

3. The Unfulfillable Order Refund Engine Actual Implementation

When a customer pays successfully, but the order cannot be fulfilled (e.g., kitchen closed, order timeout exceeded, or item out of stock):

[PAYMENT SUCCESS + CANNOT FULFILL]
↓ Backend initiates automated refund
FastAPI invokes _paytm_initiate_refund()
↓ Calls Paytm Refund API: POST /refund/apply
Record inserted into refunds with status PENDING
↓ Paytm validates and returns ACCEPTED / TXN_ACCEPTED
Paytm initiates banking reversal (1–3 banking days)
↓ Paytm S2S Refund Webhook: POST /webhooks/paytm/refund
Database updated to SUCCESS • Customer notified

4. Asynchronous Refund Semantics: "Requested ≠ Completed" Paytm Official

A common architectural flaw in naive payment integrations is treating a successful HTTP response from the Refund API as confirmation that the customer received money. In official Paytm payment gateway semantics:

1. PENDING / ACCEPTED
Paytm has accepted the refund request. Funds are queued for banking settlement. The merchant balance is reserved, but funds have not yet arrived in customer bank.
2. TXN_SUCCESS / SUCCESS
Banking partner/NPCI has successfully credited the customer account or source UPI handle. Confirmed via Refund Webhook or Refund Status API.
3. TXN_FAILURE / FAILED
The refund was rejected (e.g. beneficiary account frozen or invalid merchant balance). Requires manual intervention or secondary payout mechanism.

V Foods • Technical Architecture Whitepaper Page 6 — Concurrency Safety & Fault Resilience

Page 6 — Refunds, Concurrency & Fault Resilience

Deterministic Keys, Rush-Hour Stock Race Conditions & Crash Recovery Across 5 Lifecycle Phases

1. Payment & Stock Concurrency Race Condition Actual Implementation

Scenario: Two customers pay for the single remaining item simultaneously via Paytm UPI.

User A Payment SUCCESS (₹120)
User B Payment SUCCESS (₹120)
↓ Concurrent Webhooks hit FastAPI ↓
PostgreSQL Procedure: verify_and_record_payment()
Executes: SELECT stock_qty FROM menu_items WHERE id = ... FOR UPDATE
↓ Row Lock Serializes Execution ↓
Transaction 1 (User A)
Evaluates stock_qty = 1 >= 1
Decrements stock_qty → 0
Order CONFIRMED
Transaction 2 (User B)
Waits on lock, then reads stock_qty = 0
Sets v_refund_needed = TRUE
Triggers AUTO-REFUND

Guarantee: PostgreSQL pessimistic row-level locking (FOR UPDATE) ensures that physical inventory can never drop below zero. The losing customer is automatically refunded.

2. Deterministic Keys & Timeout Handling Actual Implementation

Deterministic Idempotency Key:

  • When invoking the Paytm Refund API, the backend calculates:
    refId = f"refund-{payment_id}"
  • This unique reference is stored under refunds.refund_ref with a database-level UNIQUE index.
  • If a network timeout occurs while transmitting to Paytm, retrying with the identical refId guarantees that Paytm will reject duplicate debit attempts and return the existing refund status.

Linking to Original Transaction:

  • Refund requests explicitly supply txnId: payments.paytm_txn_id and orderId: payments.paytm_order_id.
  • Partial refunds are supported by transmitting the calculated unfulfillable amount.

3. Server Crash Resilience Matrix Across 5 Discrete Lifecycle Phases

Failure Phase System State & Impact Automated Recovery Mechanism
Phase 1: Crash Before Gateway Payment Order inserted as awaiting_payment; user never paid or completed transaction. Order expires automatically after 10 minutes (expires_at < NOW()). No financial charge occurred.
Phase 2: Crash After Payment / Before Webhook Customer debited at Paytm; V Foods backend offline when webhook dispatches. 1. Paytm webhook retry engine re-sends payload upon server restart.
2. Background reconcile cron polls /v3/order/status and confirms order.
Phase 3: Crash During Webhook Execution Backend dies during execution of stored procedure; DB transaction uncommitted. PostgreSQL rolls back uncommitted transaction. Paytm receives no 200 OK and retries webhook. Entire procedure re-executes idempotently.
Phase 4: Crash Before Refund API Invocation Payment verified as unfulfillable (out of stock), but server dies before calling Paytm Refund API. Payment record remains marked status = 'PENDING' with failure_reason = 'OUT_OF_STOCK'. The reconcile cron detects stuck refund and executes _paytm_initiate_refund().
Phase 5: Crash During Refund Webhook Processing Paytm processed refund, but V Foods crashed before marking refunds.status = 'SUCCESS'. Reconciliation task POST /admin/refunds/reconcile polls Paytm Refund Status API (/refund/status) and completes database update.
